column1: # WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AND THE 2026-10-11 ONE DOES NOT CARRY ITS OWN ROWS.
# UNREACHABLE" and "the other 15 are NOT yet fixed and are listed here so the
# next pass has the measurement rather than the inference" -- but that file has
# had 24 lines and ZERO data rows since the commit that created it. The rows
# were never written, so CLAUDE.md was pointing the next pass at nothing. This
# redoes the measurement over all 101 candidates (not just the 42 literal ones)
# METHOD, and the two corrections it needed.
# 1. For each candidate whose URL is a complete literal, ask the upstream the
#    SAME question with a tenfold limit and compare record counts
#    (verify_feeds' own count_json/count_feed/count_csv, so a record means here
#    what it means to the rest of the tree).
# 2. THAT TEST ALONE OVER-REPORTS, and od_udata_pt.c is the proof: it answered
#    200 for one request and 2,000 for a tenfold ask, which looks exactly like a
#    discard -- but od_udata_collect() already walks it with pw_walk, so its
#    page_size=200 is a PAGE SIZE. A one-request-vs-one-request comparison
#    cannot see a collector that follows pages, so every TRUNCATING candidate
#    was also read in its collector.
# 3. IT ALSO UNDER-REPORTS WHAT CAN BE DONE ABOUT ONE. The first pass filed 17
#    rows as "no next link and no offset/page parameter in the URL, so pw_walk
#    would have to INVENT one" and left them. That reads pw_walk's rule 2
#    backwards: it will not invent a parameter, but it WILL advance one the
#    author wrote, and 11 of those 17 upstreams document a continuation their
#    collector simply never asked for ($skip, skip, start, startIndex, page).
#    So each was asked whether it HONOURS that parameter -- page 2 compared
#    against page 1, record by record -- and the honoured ones had it written
#    into the URL deliberately. One parameter was accepted and ignored (EONET's
#    offset returns page 1 again), which is why this is measured and not
#    reasoned: writing it would have made the walk re-emit page 1 twenty times.
# RESULT: 26 of 101 truncate on a single request. 14 rows / 11 sources are now
# fixed, 12 rows carry the reason they are not, and the reasons are all
# different in kind -- a cross-page comparison, a licence, a text format, an
# upstream that refuses, a real-time tail, a firehose.
#   FIXED_PAGED_OFFSET              6   a documented offset, measured honoured
#   FIXED_BIGGER_PAGE               1   offset ignored; the limit itself was the way
#   NOT_FIXED_CROSS_PAGE            1   per-page emit would be WRONG, not just partial
#   NOT_FIXED_REALTIME_TAIL         3   pageable, but re-walking it hourly is the wrong fix
#   NOT_FIXED_TEXT_FORMAT           3   pw_walk takes a parsed JSON document
#   NOT_FIXED_UPSTREAM_REFUSES      1   "the 'Skip' query option is not supported"
#   NOT_FIXED_LICENCE               1   bulk reuse needs a separate licence
#   NOT_FIXED_QUESTION_NOT_DISCARD  2   newest-first feed with no end to truncate
#   PAGES_ALREADY                   1   false positive of the single-request test
# MEASURED RECOVERY, every number read off a real run against a scratch DB
# (`--run <ID>`, stored = distinct uids the run wrote).
# Seven sources now reach their upstream's OWN declared total, in one run:
# Four more were paged earlier the same day on a next link the upstream
# 20-page ceiling, so each also files a truncation notice. bdc-stac is 0 both
# before and after: data.inpe.br is unreachable from the authoring container
# (SSL connect error), which the collector reports as rc=-1 rather than hiding.
# And three real-time seismic rows were raised to their served maximum and
# routed through pw_walk so that what they leave behind is STATED rather than
# TWO FINDINGS THAT GENERALISE PAST THESE ROWS.
# * TWO SERVICES IMPLEMENTING ONE SPEC DISAGREED ABOUT THE BASE INDEX. The FDSN
#   spec says `offset=1` is the first record. EMSC's fdsnws/event does that;
#   Earthquakes Canada's does NOT (offset=2 starts at the third record), and so
#   does EMSC's own mtws search. A stride written from the spec would have
#   skipped one event per page boundary, silently, on the services that are
#   0-based. Ask for offset=2 and see whether its first record is the plain
#   page's second or third -- it is one request and it is not inferable.
# * A SERVER THAT REFUSES IS DOING YOU A FAVOUR. BC's GeoServer answers
#   startIndex=500 with HTTP 400 "Cannot do natural order without a primary
#   key, please add it or specify a manual sort over existing attributes": it
#   would rather fail than hand back an arbitrary slice of an unsorted result.
#   Adding sortBy made it 200 with provably disjoint pages. A 400 on a paging
#   parameter is worth reading before it is written off as "no continuation".
# A `tenfold_ask` of 1000/2000/5000 is this test's own ceiling, not the
# upstream's total, so the shortfall on those rows is at least that large.
# `file:line` is where the limit stood when the row was MEASURED on 2026-10-18;
# the fixed rows have moved since, and their collectors carry the measurement
# in a comment beside the URL.

Publishes links[rel=next], but superseded() compares each feature against every OTHER to keep the latest per station. A per-page emit would publish superseded observations whenever the newer one lands on a later page. Needs whole-result accumulation, not a page walk.

WFS 2.0 startIndex, which GeoServer refuses without a sort: startIndex=500 answers HTTP 400 'Cannot do natural order without a primary key'. With sortBy=TENURE_NUMBER_ID it is 200 and consecutive pages share zero features. count 500->2500 so the walk finishes inside the 20-page ceiling. MEASURED 500 -> 42,277 stored across 17 pages, = the layer's own numberMatched.

offset IS honoured and is 0-BASED here (offset=2 starts at the third record), limit caps at 1000 server-side, full_count is 48,863. Paging is still the wrong fix: this row runs every 30 min, the 20-page ceiling stops at 20,000 and it would re-walk those same 20,000 twice an hour while never reaching the rest. limit 50->1000 (the server's cap) covers the window with days to spare, and it now goes through pw_walk so the bound is DISCLOSED. The backlog needs a dated window or a bulk catalogue.

offset is ACCEPTED (HTTP 200) and IGNORED: offset=50 returns the same 50 events as offset=0, so writing it would make pw_walk re-emit page 1 twenty times. limit IS honoured and unbounded in practice: one request at limit=20000 returns all 7,222 currently-open events (5 MB). Asked above the collection deliberately, and routed through pw_walk so an exactly-full page would still disclose.

GEOFON, format=text. pw_walk's fetch returns a parsed cJSON document, so a pipe-separated text body cannot go through it without an ndjson-style line-to-array adapter. Also UNMEASURED here: geofon.gfz.de resets the connection from this container, and the NRCan/EMSC base-index split below is exactly why its offset must not be assumed from the spec.

NRCan, format=text — same adapter gap as :181. Its offset IS honoured and is 0-BASED, which is NOT what the FDSN spec says and not what EMSC's fdsnws does: a stride written from the spec would have skipped one event per page boundary. Measure the base index before adding an offset here.
Same request as :188 (this line is the source_def .url); see that row.

page number, honoured; limit 50->2000 (7.2 MB a page) so 21,455 finishes in 11 pages. MEASURED 50 -> 21,455 emitted / 21,426 stored, = meta.found. The 29-record gap is the UPSTREAM's own duplicates: 29 _ids are served twice and both copies are byte-identical, which is real dedupe, not a key defect (checked by fetching all 11 pages and comparing).

Same decision as geoeo_emsc_moment_tensors.c, and note the split: this fdsnws endpoint's offset is 1-BASED (the FDSN spec) while the SAME organisation's mtws endpoint is 0-based — each was measured, not inferred. limit 300->1000 (the served maximum) and now through pw_walk, so a full page discloses. 15-minute interval against a catalogue of >1M events.
The Iceland AOI variant of :112; same change, same reason.

datos.gob.ar start, a 0-based record offset, honoured; limit 100->1000 so the series arrives whole. MEASURED 100 -> 271 stored in 1 page, = the series' own length; start=0 stays in the URL so growth past 1,000 pages rather than truncating.

CBS v3 ODataApi answers HTTP 500 "The 'Skip' query option is not supported" and ALSO refuses the query with no $top at all ("The given query is not allowed on this table"), so there is no continuation and no unbounded read. datasets.cbs.nl/odata/v1 does serve this table, but as long-format Observations rather than the wide TypedDataSet, so re-pointing is a record-shape change and a design decision, not a paging fix.
OData $skip, honoured (page 2 shares no record with page 1). $top 100->1000. MEASURED 100 -> 14,112 stored across 15 pages, = the collection's own $count=true.
Same request as :25 (this line is the source_def .url); see that row.

openFDA skip, honoured; limit raised to its documented maximum of 1000. MEASURED 100 -> 18,010 stored across 19 pages, = meta.results.total. skip caps at 25,000, so growth past that discloses rather than silently stops.

The collector's own header states the terms: polling this public Atom feed for new judgments is within the Open Justice Licence, but BULK or computational reuse of the whole corpus needs a separate licence from The National Archives — 'do not turn this into a crawler over the full archive'. per_page=50 of a newest-first feed is the question being asked. A licence bound is not a defect to fix.
joinpeertube start, a 0-based record offset, honoured; count 100->1000. MEASURED 100 -> 1,772 stored across 2 pages, = the envelope's own total.

gitlab.com public projects ordered by last_activity_at: an unbounded, constantly-reordered firehose with no end to truncate. per_page=100 is served (max), but 20 or 100 of a stream with millions of members is a sample either way, and the row's question is 'what moved recently'.
spaceflight-news-api is newest-first with a top-level next link; limit=20 on a scheduled newest-first feed is plausibly the question being asked. Depth is available if wanted.
FALSE POSITIVE of the one-request test: od_udata_collect() walks this with pw_walk, so page_size=200 is a PAGE SIZE. A single-request comparison cannot see a collector that follows pages.
